title: November 12 recap: Northwest Indiana news you may have missed today
text:
The Times, 601 W. 45th Ave. Munster, IN 46321
Just In
November 12 recap: Northwest Indiana news you may have missed today
Don't miss Wednesday's most popular stories from The Times.
(10) updates to this series since
Hoosier parents of children with autism soon may encounter a changed landscape when it comes to accessing a popular therapy for managing autism symptoms.
Physician assistant students at Valparaiso University are getting to learn the human body with the help of mixed virtual reality.
Urban Air opened its second Northwest Indiana location, leaping into the Valparaiso market with a new trampoline park.
Wendy’s will shutter hundreds of underperforming restaurants nationwide, but local franchisee Barney Enterprises says all Region locations will remain open.
A union said the $832 million data center under construction in Michigan City should be creating local jobs for Indiana workers instead of bringing in out-of-state workers.
Daniel Aguilar Ramirez is in custody at the Porter County Jail on allegations he was dealing in cocaine. He is also lacks permanent legal status, according to ISP.
The retro design is a callback to the 1968 state police car. Since then, ISP has changed its design several times but has used the all-white car since 2006.
GARY — The Gary/Chicago International Airport is continuing to update its facilities in anticipation of the return of commercial passenger ser…
Dutch Bros Coffee, a popular drive-thru chain from Oregon, plans to open in Munster and Valparaiso as drive-thru coffee competition heats up across the Region.
A new contract gives Merrillville police a 10% raise in 2026, boosts specialty and longevity pay, and expands take-home vehicle use.
